kf: **Chondrodermatitis nodularis helicis (CNH)** is a painful nodule on the ear rim (helix or antihelix) from pressure.
Typically older men; painful when lying on that side at night; central crust or scale.
Must be distinguished from **SCC** and BCC: biopsy if atypical.
Pressure relief is key: a pillow with a hole or ear protector; potent or intralesional steroid; surgery if persistent.
myths: **"An ear nodule is just a wart"**: painful helical nodules are usually CNH, but SCC must be excluded.
patho_lead: CNH is **pressure ischaemia** of thin skin over cartilage.

mech.t: Sleeping on the ear compresses skin against cartilage with a poor blood supply.
Skin and perichondrium are damaged; cartilage degenerates.
Degenerate collagen is pushed out through a central ulcer or crust.

mech.cap: A cut-out pillow or ear protector relieves pressure.

histo: Central ulcer with degenerate collagen and perichondrial fibrosis; acanthotic edges.
comp: Persistent pain and sleep disturbance; recurrence.
prog: Good with pressure relief; recurrence common.
